summary: M.S. Computer Engineering graduate from Rochester Institute of Technology (RIT), NY, with hands-on experience in high-performance and parallel computing: CUDA kernel optimization, MPI distributed systems on SLURM-managed clusters, and Linux-based performance profiling. Delivered up to 30× speedup in MPI-parallelized workloads and ~35% speedup in custom CUDA kernels through memory coalescing and load-imbalance analysis.

experience.title: Research Fellowship
bullets: Engineered a custom data pipeline for the BraTS 2020 multi-modal MRI dataset with batch-loading memory management for large-scale 3D volumetric inputs.
Trained U-Net segmentation with VGG-16, VGG-19, and ResNet-50 backbones; reported accuracy-latency trade-offs for deployment.

projects.name: CUDA Kernel Optimization for VGG16 Inference
bullets: Coalesced kernel ran at 49.2ms vs 73.3ms (uncoalesced) and 77.5ms (CPU TorchScript) — ~35% speedup over naive GPU with identical classification accuracy.
Replaced TorchScript conv layers in VGG16 with custom CUDA C++ kernels using memory coalescing and constant memory, eliminating per-layer allocation overhead.

projects.name: MPI Hodgkin-Huxley Neuron Simulation
bullets: Achieved up to 10.49× speedup with 12 slave processes; identified load-imbalance effects showing up to 65% performance degradation under uneven work distribution.
Implemented distributed dendrite computations across MPI workers with synchronous soma updates on a SLURM-managed cluster.

projects.name: Parallel Ray Tracer with MPI Task Scheduling
bullets: Achieved up to 30× speedup with static strip partitioning (55 processes); demonstrated dynamic task queue outperformed all static methods under unpredictable workloads.
Implemented and benchmarked four parallel work-distribution strategies (static strip/block/cyclic, dynamic task queue) for rendering 5000×5000 pixel scenes using MPI.

projects.name: SLM Compression and Benchmarking for Edge Deployment
bullets: Profiled peak VRAM and inference latency across prompt types using pynvml and psutil on Linux.
Reduced GPU memory footprint by ~55% via 8-bit quantization on TinyLlama 1.1B with <1% accuracy degradation — near-lossless compression.
